text:
morgan: ping — customer (Acme AI) opened a high-priority ticket: embeddings endpoint sometimes returns 768-dim vectors and sometimes 1536-dim for the same model. They see it correlate with traffic bursts.
liam: ugh, not 'dim flip' again. do we have their request samples?
sophie: got the sample. they use the /v1/embeddings route with model `open-embed-xlarge-v2` and our SDK v0.9.2. payload always same. sometimes batch returns 1536, sometimes 768. they attached curl + base64 vectors.
acme-support: repro steps from customer: 1) fire 120 concurrent requests of size 1 over ~6s 2) set header `X-Client-Rate: 120` (they simulate) 3) intermittently ~5% responses show 768 length, others 1536.
liam: can you paste the SDK call? might be toggling model variant or hitting a fallback.
morgan: here's a trimmed repro from their logs:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Client-Rate: 120
{ "model": "open-embed-xlarge-v2", "input": "hello" }
```
response shapes seen:
```
{ "embedding": [0.003, ...] }  // length 1536
{ "embedding": [0.001, ...] }  // length 768
```
liam: interesting — our routing can fallback to quantized/half variants when there's pressure. but that shouldn't change dimension. that suggests a mixed-model route (two different underlying models) or a padding/truncation bug in the coalescer.
sophie: i checked request logs for their org. we have coalescing enabled on the embeddings shard they hit. max_batch_size config for that pool is 128, coalesce_window is 20ms. during the bursts, autoscaler moved some shards and we saw split routing to a replica group with `variant=compact-embed` (legacy) which is 768 dim.
liam: ok that matches: mixed route hitting both new and legacy models. why would fallback be chosen? should be same model id. look at Router decision log: `X-Route-Decision: policy=latency, candidate=pool-embed-us-east-1a, fallbacks=[compact-embed]`.
morgan: customer insists they always request `open-embed-xlarge-v2`. header analysis shows correct model id. the Router selected an alt because pool reported degraded headroom.
sophie: alt model shouldn't be allowed for embeddings route that requires dimension lock. policy bug: `allow_compat_fallback=true` was set at pool-level for that customer during a temporary capacity experiment. that leaked to production for a subset of traffic.
acme-support: is there an immediate mitigation? they're seeing downstream indexing break when dims mismatch.
liam: quick mitigations:
- disable allow_compat_fallback for that pool (done, pushed 1718501252)
- add runtime check to reject responses with wrong dim and return 502 to caller instead of silently returning 768 (patch PR 4821 in flight)
- temporary routing rule to pin their org to pool-embed-stable (rolled at 1718501268)
morgan: also throttled their burst to smooth coalescing (customer approved).
sophie: for postmortem: reproduce locally by toggling `allow_compat_fallback` and triggering coalesce window + autoscaler shuffle. repro script attached by customer (they ran it with k6). recommended long-term fixes:
- ensure model dimension is part of route compatibility check (reject fallback if dims differ)
- audit pool-level experiments not to leak to prod orgs
- add telemetry metric `embed_reply_dim_mismatch` and an alerting rule
liam: I dug into the batcher code: when batch splits across shard boundaries during a coalesce flush, we reassign requests to shard replicas. there's a race where variant metadata wasn't preserved in one code path — PR ready to patch.
infra-bot: deploy: rollout patch-router-metadata-fix to prod (canary 10%) at 1718501285 :rocket:
morgan: customer notified of mitigation and ETA for permanent fix (told them 24h). they want a reproducible test to run against their CI: i shared a k6 script + env var to force shard shuffle.
acme-support: thanks — they validated that after the pin + throttle, all embeddings returned 1536 consistently.
liam: follow-ups: create an Ops runbook for embedding-dim-fallback, add an abort-on-dim-mismatch feature in SDK, and schedule a postmortem.
sophie: filing internal ticket INF-1129 for telemetry + unit tests.
morgan: closing loop with product and CS. thx everyone :thumbsup:
